key_insight: Grokking is explained as a geometry-driven transition in parameter space: optimization with Adam plus weight shrinkage creates an outer initialization shell, a middle memorization shell, and an inner generalization core.
engineering_relevance: The paper gives practical scaling laws for learning rate, batch size, and L2 regularization that can help predict and control delayed generalization in training runs.
method: Theoretical shell-core topology analysis of reachable solutions under Adam with weight shrinkage.
Stopping-time theory to model when trajectories escape memorization and enter the generalization region.
Derivation of grokking scaling laws and comparison with prior results.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports empirical evidence for the shell-core geometry and experiments validating the derived scaling laws against prior literature.
watch_item: The theory is tied to a specific optimization setup (Adam with shrinkage regularization), so its behavior may not transfer unchanged to other optimizers or training regimes.
paper_title: A Stochastic--Geometric Theory of Scaling Laws in Grokking
